reasoning: Preserved all four failure-driven edits. The success-driven category fallback overlaps with the failure guidance to use category listings when available and inspect remaining pages, so it is deduplicated rather than added separately.

edits.target: 3. Shorten unsuccessful multiword queries to a keyword or synonym. Do not paste full product titles: drop curly quotes, dashes, degree signs and similar characters, and search with a few distinctive keywords.
edits.content: For attribute-heavy searches, do not rely on one compound query containing every requirement. Search the product type or relevant category, then search distinctive brands, model families, and attribute terms separately; inspect results for equivalent wording and values that differ from the query. Use category listings as an additional discovery route when available. For cheapest-offer searches with noisy or broad results, inspect plausible candidates that could beat the current best, including remaining result pages as needed; do not consider a shop checked based only on the cheapest item encountered in a broad keyword search.

For lighting requirements, distinguish lighting built into the product from support for connecting or controlling separate lights. An RGB header, RGB Fusion compatibility, or support for RGB LED strips alone does not establish that the motherboard itself has RGB lighting; count it only if the task accepts RGB-device support or the product evidence confirms the requested lighting feature.

edits.target: For tasks asking for all qualifying offers or every offer tied at a maximum, keep a per-shop ledger of candidates, specifications, and exact offer URLs. After identifying a plausible product, search its distinctive model name or part number in each shop as well as using the general product/category query; equivalent models may have separate shop offers even when a generic query misses them. Count each shop’s relevant results and inspect its remaining pages before concluding that no other qualifying offer exists.
edits.content: Treat relevant related-product links as discovery leads, not as search-result counts: open plausible candidates and verify the requirements on that offer itself. Before submitting, review the ledger for qualifying variants and every offer tied at the best price; do not submit only the first qualifying model or only one member of a tie.

edits.target: At `<shop>/checkout/`, fill billing and card fields by label. Check default Country / Region and State / County against the task address; change mismatches using their inner search fields and matching options. Complete checkout with **Place order**, then verify that an order-received confirmation appears before proceeding to final submission.
edits.content: If requested items are in different shops, each shop has its own cart and checkout. Complete and verify an order for every shop containing a requested item; do not treat confirmation of one shop’s order as completion of the whole task. Navigate to the solution page and submit only after all required orders are confirmed.
